elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4 as rendered: "Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ... for convenience at the end of any calendar month". The Service Option Attachments are the Order-Form-referenced attachments, so the Agreement-or-order-level right is present. (The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a pattern artifact — the operative text expressly grants the right; the regex appears keyed to notice wording rather than the grant.)

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: 3.4(a) requires "at least one month's prior written notice" and 3.4 permits termination only "at the end of any calendar month". A calendar month may exceed 30 days, and the month-end effective-date constraint can push the elapsed period well beyond 30 days (e.g., notice on 2 January cannot take effect before 28/29 February). Read literally this is not a 30-day right, though it is materially better than the 60–90 day fallback window.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 3.4 nor the surrounding rendered text contains any refund obligation; 3.4 only imposes a payment obligation on Customer (early termination charges). No pro-rata prepaid-fee refund exists to be inferred.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: IBM's only mid-term exit in the rendered text is Section 3.3 termination for uncured material breach; its only other exit is the Section 3.2 notice at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term, which operates solely to defeat automatic renewal. No mid-term no-cause IBM right appears in the cited operative language.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 3.4 plus 3.4(a) give Customer an unconditional convenience exit on "at least one month's prior written notice", effective at the end of a calendar month. The notice burden is shorter than, and therefore more favourable to Customer than, the 60–90 day fallback ceiling; the element's protective purpose (a Customer convenience right requiring no more than 90 days' notice) is satisfied.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Redlined 3.4(b) now reads "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, not to exceed three (3) months' charges." The cap is unconditional and applies to the whole early-termination charge, closing the previously open-ended penalty.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 3.2 is a pure non-renewal mechanic: the Attachment "will renew automatically ... unless either party notifies ... at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term ... that it has elected to terminate". The election operates only on renewal, so the Attachment ends at the expiry of the then-current term; no other IBM no-cause exit exists (3.3 is breach-only). Natural-term non-renewal is otherwise a RENEWAL matter, correctly not double-flagged here.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 3.2 requires written notice "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — the 90-day floor applies to IBM as well as Customer.

reasons: Fallback is complete after the single edit: the only operative change is the addition of "not to exceed three (3) months' charges" in 3.4(b), which supplies the one missing fallback element (fee cap). Customer's convenience right, the term-end-only IBM exit and the 90-day IBM notice were already present in the original text.

Preferred is not reached for two reasons the drafter should note but need not pursue: (i) there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund on Customer convenience termination, and (ii) the month-end effective-date restriction plus "one month's" notice can exceed 30 days. Neither is required now that the fallback is complete.

Minimality holds: no favourable language was deleted ("if any", the prerequisite-Attachment carve-out, the Attachment A cross-reference and Section 3.3's reference to "the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b)" all survive intact), no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra remedy was added, and no term outside the fee-cap element was touched.

Intent preserved: the cap sits inside the existing 3.4(b) payment condition, so Section 3.3's proviso barring IBM from recovering 3.4(b) charges after its own breach remains coherent, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Optional tightening (not required for completeness): "three (3) months' charges" leaves the base implicit; if Attachment A prices vary, consider "three (3) months of the then-current monthly recurring charges for the terminated Service Option Attachment" to foreclose IBM computing the cap off a larger charge base, particularly given its Section 13.1 change right flagged in the rationale.

Deterministic checks reviewed in substance: the failing "Customer convenience termination present" regex is contradicted by the rendered Section 3.4 grant and does not indicate a drafting defect; the coverage and minimality gates pass consistently with the analysis above.

Finding status "deviation" is correct — pre-redline the clause failed the fallback on the uncapped early-termination charge, which is a material term, so a redline rather than a rationale-only note was warranted.
